claims.text: Detection of entailment and contradiction relations between texts is a minimal metric for evaluating text understanding systems.
Intensionality is widespread in natural language.
Intensionality raises detection issues for text understanding systems.
A contexted clausal representation derived from formal semantics permits tractable detection of an extended range of intensional entailments and contradictions.

evidence.description: The authors argue that the detection of entailment and contradiction relations between texts is a minimal metric for the evaluation of text understanding systems.
The authors state that intensionality is widespread in natural language.
The authors state that intensionality raises a number of detection issues that cannot be brushed aside.
The paper describes a contexted clausal representation, derived from formal semantics, that permits an extended range of intensional entailments and contradictions to be tractably detected.

methodologies.name: Contexted clausal representation
methodologies.description: A representation derived from formal semantics that allows tractable detection of intensional entailments and contradictions.

limitations.text: Intensionality in natural language raises detection issues that complicate text understanding evaluation.
